messages:
mira: Heads-up — CrestlinePay on Dedicated reported p99 latency spikes starting 08:12 UTC. Customer sees 5x above SLA. Marking P0 and requesting immediate cross-team commitments. @alex @noah please advise current rollout state and any active canaries.

alex: On it. Canary 3 is running on pool-dedicated-2, traffic ~8%. No config changes this morning. Initial metrics show queueing at the frontend proxy. Investigating whether batching/kv-cache pressure caused it. :eyes:

noah: I can take the kernel/runtime angle. Last change to scheduling landed in #4219, but that was for short-lived seq len corner cases. I haven't seen regressions in perf tests. Pulling logs now.

sam: Ops: we've already elevated to incident bridge with CrestlinePay. They need a temporary routing fallback to the lower-cost model variant to keep latency within SLA while we triage. Who can own the routing policy change?

mira: Need owner for routing fallback + timeline. Also need a short-term mitigation (30m) and a plan for full fix (3 business days).

eva: I can own routing fallback. Plan: shift 30% of traffic to model-variant-v4 (cpu-quant) which is compatible and lower-latency for their payloads. Will submit PR to traffic-config repo and request emergency deploy. ETA 15m.

alex: Thanks @eva. Can you post the exact policy snippet? Ops needs to review. I also want to run a quick perf profile against pool-dedicated-2 while fallback rolls.

eva: Pushing snippet here:
```
route: {
  match: { customer_id: "crestlinepay" },
  actions: [
    { type: "split", weights: [{variant: "primary", w: 70}, {variant: "model-variant-v4", w: 30}] }
  ]
}
```
I'll attach PR in 5.

noah: While that's happening I'll start a targeted mem/kv cache pressure test on the pod set. If we see increased hot-kv eviction it's likely cache thrash.

sam: Devops-bot: please record the deploy and notify the oncall after PR merged.

devops-bot: noted. Creating emergency deploy runbook entry (incident 2026-17198). Will ping oncall.

mira: Ownership summary: @eva = routing fallback + PR, @noah = runtime profiling & logs, @alex = perf comparison + canary watch, @sam = customer comms/bridge. Full fix owner TBD (likely runtime team).

alex: Quick ask: can someone sanity-check the canary rollback command?

noah: Use this to revert to prior kernel optimizations if perf degrades:
```bash
kubectl annotate deployment svc-runtime kernel-opt=previous --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deployment svc-runtime
```
Tested in staging.

eva: PR #4873 created: traffic-config/crestlinepay-fallback. Tagging @sam for approval.

sam: Approved. Deploying now. Will update CrestlinePay that we expect a 15m window to stabilize.

mira: Timeline checkpoints: +15m fallback in place, +30m initial perf check, +3h triage blamestorm and root-cause hypothesis, +72h hotfix/patch plan. Set reminders and update the incident doc.

alex: I'll post perf numbers to the incident doc after 30m. If latency still high after fallback we'll ramp to 50% and open the rollback play.

noah: Found initial hint — pod logs show repeated KV fetch misses for long contexts. If validated, we may change prefix cache sizing which touches many runtime bits. That is why we need the 72h window.

mira: OK. Closing loop: owners confirmed, PR + deploy underway. Please ping here with any blockers. :thumbsup:
